Elastic Load Balancer

The topic is now confirmed by the project owner, so the technical article is populated. The canonical ledger status is not promoted until the original published artifact is recovered.

Elastic Load Balancing introduced a stable traffic-distribution layer in front of multiple targets so application instances can be replaced and scaled without clients tracking each server directly.

Architecture / mental model

clients → AWS load balancer listeners → target group → healthy application targets across subnets/AZs

How it works

Elastic Load Balancing is the AWS service family for distributing traffic across registered targets. The exact behavior depends on load-balancer type, but the core pattern is listener → routing decision → target group → healthy target.

Health checks matter because the load balancer should avoid sending normal traffic to targets that fail the configured health criteria. A running EC2 instance and a healthy application target are not the same fact.

For web applications, Application Load Balancers provide HTTP/HTTPS-aware routing features, while other load-balancer types serve different network needs. The architectural lesson is to choose based on protocol and routing behavior, not simply 'I need a load balancer.'

Hands-on reference

aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers
aws elbv2 describe-target-groups
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn TARGET_GROUP_ARN

Verification

Send repeated requests through the load balancer, take one backend unhealthy in a lab and inspect target-health state while confirming healthy targets continue serving traffic.

Field note / gotcha

A target can be alive at the OS level and still fail the load balancer health check because the wrong path, port, protocol or application dependency is configured.

Security considerations

Terminate TLS deliberately, restrict backend Security Groups to the load balancer where appropriate and protect health/admin endpoints from becoming public information leaks.

What I learned

Load balancing separates client identity from individual server identity, but health semantics decide whether that abstraction is useful.
